newsitem.title: UK: Mediterranean oil products mixed, fuel strongest.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean oil products mixed, fuel strongest.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Friday.
Naphtha prices held steady supported against weaker crude futures by perceptions of underlying petrochemical demand and amid scarce offers of product, traders said.

However buyers remained fairly relaxed with a 60kt Algerian cargo that was on offer all week at cif high +$3 now being taken transatlantic according to the holder Petrobras after failing to find buyers in Europe.
Gasoline prices were soft as recently supportive crude and products futures lost ground in late trade on Friday.
Poor reforming margins continued to cap refinery output of higher octane grades and low octane supplies continued to grow.
Some buying was seen into Italy for premuim 0.15 leaded barrels but outright prices were hard to pin down.
Gas oil was steady to softer with the market under pressure from ample Russian supplies.
Premiums for Russian cargoes sank from quotes cif high +$3 a tonne to +50 cents to $1 this week.
At least one first half cargo and two second half cargoes were still on offer after four distressed pieces traded on Thursday.
Good demand for inferior spec heating oil was seen into the eastern Mediterranean.
Fuel oil was firm amid a perception of tight supply in the cracked markets. But straight-run suplies grew.
An Italian cargo, of slightly poor quality, was confirmed sold on Thursday to a trader at $1 over the quoted fob high.

Another refiner was heard buying an Odessa-origin M-40 cargo from a trader on Thursday at a quotes-related price. Another part-cargo M-40 was also traded, at $4.50 over the quoted cif high, cif Genoa.
